questions.solution_en:
Through - moving in one side and out of the other side of (an opening, channel, or location).

As per the meaning, delivering letters through hand does not give a meaningful sentence.

We use 'by + noun' to describe how someone travels or communicates, or how things are processed.

So, in the given sentence, 'through' should be replaced with 'by' to rectify the error.

The correct sentence is: The postman delivers the letters by hand, door to door.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note:

Coordinating conjunctions join items that are of equal importance in a sentence. Also, it joins two words of equal grammatical rank.

Examples include: And, but, nor, or, but, otherwise, also, either-or, neither-nor, etc. are the chief coordinate conjunctions.

Subordinating conjunctions connect subordinate clauses (dependent clauses) to the main clause of a sentence.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The salesperson wanted to know what my favourite lunch was.
options_en: The salesperson said, "What is your favourite lunch?"
The salesperson said, "What has been your favourite lunch?"
The salesperson said, "What having been your favourite lunch?"
The salesperson said, "What was your favourite lunch?"
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", and "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech are changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Simple Present tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Simple Past tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'wanted to know' becomes 'said', 'my' becomes 'your', and 'was' becomes 'is'.

Accordingly, the option that has the correct Direct speech form of the given sentence is option (a), The salesperson said, "What is your favourite lunch?"

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The man said to me, "May your child never know a hungry belly"
options_en: The man blessed me that my child will never know a hungry belly.
The man wished me that his child may never know a hungry belly.
The man wished me that my child might never know a hungry belly.
The man prayed for me that my child could never have known a hungry belly.
questions.solution_en:
These kinds of sentences are called Optative Sentences.

Optative Sentences are usually prayers or wishes.

In these kinds of sentences, "said" in the Direct Speech is changed into "prayed", "wished", etc.

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

While changing from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech, the sentence is changed into its Assertive form i.e., "Subject + might/may + V1 + Object".

For example:

The father said to his son, "May God bless you!" (Direct Speech)

The father wished his son that God might bless him. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'wished'.

· 'May' is changed into 'might'.

· The possessive determiner 'your' is changed into 'my'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): The man wished me that my child might never know a hungry belly.

options_en: The ancient Roman aqueducts was engineered to transport water over very long distances.

questions.solution_en:

This sentence correctly uses the passive voice of the simple past tense ("were engineered"). The passive is required because the subject ("aqueducts") is the receiver of the action (engineered). The plural subject "aqueducts" correctly pairs with the plural verb "were."

· Option (a): This has a subject-verb agreement error. The plural subject "aqueducts" requires the plural verb "were," not the singular verb "was."

· Option (c): This is grammatically incorrect. The passive voice requires the past participle ("engineered"), not the base form "engineer."

· Option (d): This is an incorrect passive construction. The past perfect passive would be "had been engineered."

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

The teacher said, "Mahatma Gandhi was born in Gujarat." (Direct Speech)

The teacher said that Mahatma Gandhi was born in Gujarat. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Inverted commas are removed. And, 'that' is introduced in the sentence.

So, the sentence in indirect speech is: The tutor said that the world war first began in 1914.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

He will receive the scholarship in the next semester.
options_en: The scholarship will received by him in the next semester.
The scholarship is being received by him in the next semester.
The scholarship will be received by him in the next semester.
He will be received by the scholarship in the next semester.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option (c).

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a 'to be' form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The scholarship will be received by him in the next semester.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is error free, mark 'No error' as your answer.

No sooner had she crossed a small bridge near the farm when/ the storm resumed/ with even greater intensity.
options_en: No sooner had she crossed a small bridge near the farm when
questions.solution_en:
Some adverbs are used in pairs- 'Hardly..when', 'no sooner.. than', 'scarcely..when', 'so..that', etc. So, the use of 'when' is inappropriate here. 'No sooner' is used to show that one thing happens immediately after another thing, so its usage seems appropriate here. It should be replaced with 'than'.

Alternatively, 'no sooner' can be replaced with 'hardly/scarcely'.

Hence, option (a) is correct.
